shouldFix.risk: The successor's finding ledger is the durable proof that every frozen predecessor item was repaired, carried, or consciously left advisory. An explicit empty array silently erases a finding and makes later convergence checks report a false predecessor set. This is the same bookkeeping class that earlier successors treated as SHOULD-FIX.

shouldFix.title: The new closed cartesian corpus conflicts with component-manifest platform scope
shouldFix.measurement: componentLane and the live DR-G16 row make relevant-platform scope component-manifest-specific. coverageLaw instead defines applicability as every cell in a closed component × language-role × platform × changeClass cartesian product. A component-specific platform set is a dependent domain, not an ordinary global cartesian factor, and the text does not say which reading controls. The only blocked-cell carve-out is for a D-002-deferred role/platform, not for a platform simply absent from one component's manifest.
shouldFix.counterexample: Component A declares only macOS and component B declares only Linux, both lawful under the manifest-scoped lane contract. If platform is the union {macOS, Linux}, the stated cartesian product requires A×Linux and B×macOS cells even though neither platform is relevant for that component. If those cells are omitted, coverageLaw fails; if executed, the harness exceeds the live row's manifest scope; and no D-002-deferred standing applies merely because a component did not declare that platform.
shouldFix.risk: The v5 wording closes the old undefined-applicability escape by replacing it with an over-broad or mathematically ambiguous matrix. It does not permit unsafe under-selection, so this is not a blocker, but it does leave the G16 corpus non-portable and potentially unsatisfiable for heterogeneous component manifests.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Define a closed dependent product explicitly, for example {(component, role, platform, changeClass) | role and platform are declared for that component}, plus separately enumerated D-002-deferred slots and reasons. Preserve the omission-fails rule inside that exact domain.

shouldFix.title: The new multi-component predicate is absent from clauses that claim to enumerate the closed authority and custody roster
shouldFix.measurement: The specific v5 field says multiComponentSharedLaneSelection is part of the ownership record with the same custody, completeness, and self-change, and selectorDecision.inputsDigest includes it. But selector.authority still says the ownership record 'includes' only unit maps, shared-surface consumer edges, and comparison basis. inputCompleteness calls unit maps, sharedSurfaceConsumers, and DR-103 edges the 'one closed authority roster'. ID-DEP-C6 likewise defines custody bytes as unit maps + sharedSurfaceConsumers plus dependency edges. None names the new predicate.

The component set reaches cardinality two but SL-2/SL-3/SL-4 do not fire. The specific algorithm and G16-5 make that implementation nonconforming, while the clauses that call themselves the closed input/custody roster do not classify the omitted predicate as missing or AMBIGUOUS.
shouldFix.risk: The operative predicate, digest, fixpoint, and G16 class make the intended answer recoverable, so the v4 blocker is repaired. The remaining contradictory exhaustiveness claims are nevertheless authority-bearing blueprint inputs and must agree before implementation is authorized.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Add multiComponentSharedLaneSelection to selector.authority, inputCompleteness, and ID-DEP-C6; state explicitly whether a missing/conflicting predicate forces REFUSE or may select the complete universe; and roster those paths in the successor.

shouldFix.title: The selector output enum cannot encode a lawful multi-owner conflict resolved by REFUSE
shouldFix.measurement: Multiple owners produce AMBIGUOUS-CONFLICT. The policy still lists REFUSE and SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE as options, the fail-safe permits typed refusal, and G16-3 says a complete-universe conflict 'may' select the universe rather than requiring it. Yet the output enum is only none | refuse-only | conflict-universe. It has no value for conflict + refuse: refuse-only asserts the wrong ambiguity class, while conflict-universe asserts the other resolution.
shouldFix.counterexample: A changed unit has two owners and the comparison-basis universe is independently complete. The selector conservatively chooses the lawful REFUSE option. It emits no lanes and a typed refusal, but cannot populate ambiguity without falsely saying either that the condition was REFUSE-only or that it resolved by universe selection.
shouldFix.risk: Refusal remains fail-safe, so this is not an under-selection blocker. It does prevent selectorDecision from carrying an exact, auditably typed account of every lawful policy branch, weakening the evidence contract v5 otherwise repaired.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Separate ambiguityClass = none | refuse-only | conflict from resolution = none | refuse | universe and constrain lawful pairs, or add a distinct conflict-refuse value. If complete conflicts are instead required to select the universe, say MUST rather than may/default and remove REFUSE from that branch.
